chunks: Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام:
A man asked him, while he was present, about a man who comes out of the bathhouse or performs ghusl, then wraps himself and wears his shirt over his lower garment, and prays in that state. He said:

"This is from the practice of the people of Lut." I said: "He wraps himself over the shirt." He said: "This is from arrogance." I said: "The shirt is thin, and he covers himself with it." He said: "This, along with unfastening buttons during salat, flicking pebbles, and chewing frankincense in gatherings and on the roadway, is from the practice of the people of Lut."

And a concession regarding wrapping oneself with the lower garment over the shirt has been narrated from al-'Abd al-Salih عليه السلام, from Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام, and from Abu Ja'far al-Thani عليه السلام; and according to it I hold and give fatwa.

key_terms.الْأَزْرَارِ: buttons or fastenings of the garment
key_terms.الْحَمَّامِ: the bathhouse from which a person exits before dressing and praying
key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: a concession or allowance in the ruling
key_terms.قَمِيصَهُ: his shirt or tunic worn on the body
key_terms.يَتَوَشَّحُ: he wraps himself with a garment across the body

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about wrapping an izar over a shirt during salat?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a form of dress in salat and mentions a censure of certain manners and outward behaviors. The closing statement reports a transmitted concession for wrapping the izar over the shirt and states that this is the ruling adopted for fatwa.
